cases.about: A large JPEG and a PNG get WebP and recompressed copies in optimised/ in one command the person allows; the smaller is kept, bytes before and after are reported, and the SVG and the tiny icon are skipped with why.

shell.output:
/usr/bin/cwebp
/usr/bin/jpegoptim
/usr/bin/oxipng
2410112 hero.jpg
845330 team.png
312540 optimised/hero.webp
498002 optimised/hero.jpg
201004 optimised/team.webp
655120 optimised/team.png

call.command: cd "site/img" && command -v cwebp jpegoptim oxipng convert; mkdir -p optimised && [ -e optimised/hero.webp ] || cwebp -q 80 -resize 2400 0 hero.jpg -o optimised/hero.webp; [ -e optimised/hero.jpg ] || jpegoptim --dest=optimised --strip-all -m82 hero.jpg; [ -e optimised/team.webp ] || cwebp -q 80 team.png -o optimised/team.webp; [ -e optimised/team.png ] || oxipng --out optimised/team.png team.png; stat -c '%s %n' hero.jpg team.png optimised/*

script.say:
**Optimised**
- hero.jpg — 2,410,112 → 312,540 bytes (optimised/hero.webp, resized to 2400 px) — 87% smaller
- team.png — 845,330 → 201,004 bytes (optimised/team.webp) — 76% smaller

**Skipped**
- logo.svg — not a JPEG or PNG
- icon.png — under 50 KB

**Total**
- 3,255,442 → 513,544 bytes — 84% smaller

## Report
- listed 4 files, made web copies of 2 in optimised/ with one command
